novelty_filter.accepted_standard: A previously untested source-supported procedural rule, defined outcome branch, consequential timing exception or explicit action-availability exception.
rejected_as_nonadditive: Different player counts, Item colors, damage totals or Intruder counts within already-tested formulas.
Creeper/Adult or Breeder/Queen substitution within the same injury-check procedure.
Danger with every Corridor already noisy: Q08 already says to place only in Corridors lacking Noise.
Leg Wound until dressed: Q16/Q36 already test dressing suppression of Serious Wound effects.
Non-initiating trade participants exchanging: Q32 already allows agreeing Characters in the same Room to exchange.
Fire Control targeting ongoing Combat: Q38 already permits any target Room and all its Intruders; acting-character Room Action restrictions are separately covered.
Further combinations of already-tested Fire, Malfunction, Pod or endgame rules without an additional explicit source exception.
A definite ruling for an unresolved source gap, or an effect from unavailable physical cards, invented to increase coverage.

items.assessment: The Adult model freeing procedure removes only non-Combat Adults. If all eight are in Combat it supplies no executable model-availability fallback. FAQ Rules19 concerns reusable tokens, not a free model.

Queen development adds a board Egg even when the Nest has previously been marked destroyed; persistence/reset of the destruction state and Objective consequence is not explicit. The dropped-Egg non-restoration ruling does not answer this different Egg-generation case.

The if-they-miss clause does not explicitly disambiguate Contamination on a successful Egg Melee. The FAQ has no specific successful-Egg-melee ruling. Q18 preserves the limitation rather than inventing a success-hit draw, refund or unconditional waiver.

Dedicated critical moment and reference sheet say first death; the Pod overview says any death. First-death-only is the strongest detailed-rule interpretation, and subsequent normal relocking is explicitly allowed. FAQ Rules25 addresses repeated yellow Self-Destruct spaces only and cannot be cited as an express later-death ruling. Keep the discrepancy visible separately from the definite first-death case covered by Q58.

other_source_wording_notes.assessment: Retain the explicit Repairs/Tools Repair/Break exception despite Malfunction. FAQ Rooms5 is contextual shorthand about Room/state consequences, not an explicit repeal of the detailed manual exception.

Retain the detailed normal attack rule using fewest Action cards. The quick-reference wording omits the qualifier; do not silently import the separate Surprise comparison that explicitly includes Contamination.
